name: Quicken Simplifi
tagline: Import account exports and build spending plans, watchlists, and reports

pricing.notes: Typical standard monthly amount before promotions.

tiers.name: Quicken Simplifi
tiers.limits: Account aggregation, spending plan, reports, investments, projected cash flow and retirement planner; sharing with 1 additional person
tiers.notes: First-year promotional monthly equivalent, billed annually; crossed-out regular equivalent is $6.99/month. Offer ends 2026-09-11.

pricing.billingTerms: annual only; full annual charge upfront; first-year promotional pricing
pricing.hiddenCosts: Auto-renews yearly at the then-current rate. The displayed $3.99/month equivalent is a new-member first-year offer, not the renewal rate; exact annual checkout total may differ from 12× the displayed equivalent.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Quicken Simplifi, import account exports and build spending plans, watchlists, and reports. The hard boundary is bank aggregation, transaction cleaning, mobile sync, support, and mature finance workflows, plus financial integrations, compliance, and trust.
coreLoopDIY: Import account exports, categorize transactions with transparent rules, build spending plans and watchlists, reconcile balances, and export clean reports without moving money.
requirements: CSV or OFX exports from financial institutions
whatYouLose: bank aggregation, transaction cleaning, mobile sync, support, and mature finance workflows
replacementScope: personal ledger or simple invoicing tool
ongoingBurden: import normalization, reconciliation, rule drift, exchange rates, backups, audit trails, tax changes, bank APIs, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Quicken Simplifi because people pay because accurate money records and dependable institution connections are worth more than the visible charts. The recurring cost buys import normalization, reconciliation, rule drift, exchange rates, backups, audit trails, tax changes, bank APIs, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Actual Budget
priorArt.desc: Active local-first open-source personal finance application.

alternatives.name: FreeBudget
alternatives.desc: CSV imports, spending plans, rules, reports and net worth for free; live bank links cost extra.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser or installation of its progressive web app
facts.dataFormat: Transactions, budgets, rules, reports, and net-worth records live in FreeBudget's cloud; manual and CSV import/export are available, while linked-account data passes through Plaid when the paid sync option is enabled.
facts.gapVsPaid: FreeBudget's free core lacks Simplifi's automatic account refresh, recurring-bill intelligence, polished watchlists, mobile apps, and low-effort spending-plan updates.

alternatives.name: Actual Budget
alternatives.desc: Imported account data, budgets, rules and reports on your disk; watchlists become categories and schedules.

facts.install: Native desktop app for local-only use, or the official Docker/Node server for browser access and device sync
facts.dataFormat: Each client works from a local SQLite budget; the server keeps account metadata plus budget blobs under its data directory, and optional end-to-end encryption covers budget contents but not bank-sync tokens.
facts.gapVsPaid: Actual's schedules and categories can imitate watchlists, but it lacks Simplifi's turnkey bank aggregation, recurring detection, spending-plan presentation, and managed mobile sync.

alternatives.name: Firefly III
alternatives.desc: Imported transactions, budgets, recurring bills and reports in Docker; setup is not simplified.

facts.install: Official Docker Compose deployment; a separate Firefly III Data Importer is normally added for bank files
facts.dataFormat: Transactions, accounts, budgets, rules, and metadata live in the configured MariaDB/MySQL or PostgreSQL database; uploads and generated files live in persistent server volumes.
facts.gapVsPaid: Firefly III is far harder to deploy and maintain and does not match Simplifi's automatic account linking, mobile polish, watchlists, and approachable spending-plan workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is operating a real web service, Docker, a database, application secrets, TLS, mail, backups, upgrades, and usually the separate importer plus an API token.

alternatives.name: Wealthfolio
alternatives.desc: Spending, budgets, rules and net worth on your device; automatic account sync is paid.

facts.install: Native desktop or iOS app, or the official Docker image/Compose deployment for web mode
facts.dataFormat: Desktop and self-hosted modes use a local SQLite database (the web server exposes a configurable app.db path); optional Wealthfolio Connect and encrypted device sync send selected holdings/account data through the vendor service.
facts.gapVsPaid: Wealthfolio is strongest for portfolios and net worth, but its free mode lacks Simplifi's automatic transaction sync, recurring-bill detection, watchlists, and mature spending plan.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Simplifi plan and a personal ledger or simple invoicing tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Quicken Simplifi in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and local-first encryption; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: import account exports, categorize transactions with transparent rules, build spending plans and watchlists, reconcile balances, and export clean reports without moving money.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support CSV and OFX import with saved column mappings and duplicate detection.
Implement accounts, transactions, transfers, categories, payees, notes, and split transactions.
Add deterministic categorization rules whose matches can be inspected and undone.
Provide reconciliation, monthly budget, cash-flow, net-worth, and export views.
Keep an immutable import log and require explicit confirmation before destructive changes.
Encrypt local data, create automatic backups, and document restore on a fresh machine.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out initiating payments or moving money.
Deliberately leave out tax, payroll, or accounting compliance guarantees.
Deliberately leave out screen-scraped bank access and commercial institution aggregation.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
